faqs.a: For most people it lands within a few percentage points of lab methods. Hydration, posture and exact tape placement move the number around, so treat it as a screening estimate rather than a precise measurement.
faqs.q: How accurate is the Army tape test?

faqs.a: Men: neck just below the Adam's apple, abdomen horizontally around the navel. Women: neck the same way, waist at the narrowest point, hip at the widest point around the buttocks. Measure at the end of a normal exhale.

faqs.q: What are the Army body fat limits?

faqs.a: Yes. Army Regulation 600-9 sets the body composition standard, and soldiers who fail the weight-for-height screening table take the tape test at their unit.
faqs.q: Does the Army still use the tape test?

faqs.a: Yes. This calculator converts metric entries to inches automatically because the official formula works in inches.
faqs.q: Can I enter measurements in centimetres?

faqs.a: Different methods measure differently. The tape test estimates from circumferences, calipers measure skinfold thickness, and DEXA scans measure directly. Each has its own error range.
faqs.q: Why does my result differ from my gym's caliper test?

army-body-fat-calculator.formula:
Male: %BF = 86.010 x log10(abdomen - neck) - 70.041 x log10(height) + 36.76
Female: %BF = 163.205 x log10(waist + hip - neck) - 97.684 x log10(height) - 78.387
All measurements in inches; log10 is the base-10 logarithm.
howTo: Select Male or Female and pick your age group (17-20, 21-27, 28-39 or 40+).
Enter your height and your neck circumference.
Men add the abdomen measurement at the navel; women add the waist at its narrowest point and the hip at its widest.
Your estimated body fat, the maximum allowed for your group and your pass or fail result appear instantly.
keyFacts: The Army's tape-test formula comes from U.S. Navy research and is the method behind Army Regulation 600-9.
Men are measured at the neck and abdomen (navel). Women are measured at the neck, waist and hip.
The formula works in inches, so metric entries are converted automatically before calculation.
Maximum body fat rises with age: men 20% to 26%, women 30% to 36% across the four age groups.
A soldier who exceeds the weight-for-height screen at the unit takes the tape test; this calculator mirrors that same math.
Measure at the end of a normal breath with the tape snug but not compressing the skin.

limitations: The tape test is an estimate, not a measurement; DEXA or hydrostatic weighing are more accurate.
Tape placement, posture and hydration can shift the result by a couple of percentage points.
Very muscular people can fail the tape test while being lean, a known weakness of the method.
This is a general information tool, not an official military assessment or medical advice.

army-body-fat-calculator.quickAnswer: The U.S. Army tape test estimates body fat from neck, waist and hip tape measurements plus height. A 70-inch-tall man with a 34-inch abdomen and 15.5-inch neck is about 16.5% body fat, comfortably under the 24% maximum for men aged 28-39. Women are measured at the neck, waist and hip instead.
